heading.en: Moving up, moving across, moving out

hook.en: In one year a bank promotes 30 clerks to officers, *transfers* 50 staff to new branches, retires 20, accepts 15 resignations and dismisses one for fraud. Managing these movements fairly is a big part of HRM.

narration.en: In one year a bank promotes 30 clerks to officers, transfers 50 staff to new branches, retires 20, accepts 15 resignations and dismisses one for fraud. Managing these movements fairly is a big part of HRM.

say.en: In one year a bank promotes 30 clerks to officers, transfers 50 staff to new branches, retires 20, accepts 15 resignations and dismisses one for fraud. Managing these movements fairly is a big part of HRM. In this lesson: Explain promotion and its bases.
Explain transfers and demotion.
Distinguish the forms of separation.

body.en: Internal mobility is the movement of employees within the organisation. *Promotion* is moving an employee to a higher post with more responsibility, status and usually pay. It may be based on seniority (length of service), which is objective and avoids favouritism, or on merit (ability and performance), which rewards talent; many firms combine the two. Transfer is moving an employee to another job, place or shift of similar status and pay, to meet the organisation's needs, to fit the person better, to give wider experience, or as a remedy. Demotion is moving an employee to a lower post, usually as a penalty or when a post is abolished.

points.en: *Promotion*: higher post; seniority or merit basis
*Transfer*: same level, different job, place or shift
Types of *transfer*: production, replacement, versatility, shift, remedial

title.en: On the board: Forms of mobility and separation

say.en: Movements inside the firm and out of it.
On the board: Forms of mobility and separation.

body.en: *Separation* is the end of an employee's service with the organisation. Retirement is separation at the age of superannuation, or earlier by choice, such as voluntary retirement under a scheme (VRS). Resignation is voluntary separation by the employee. Lay-off is a temporary inability of the employer to give work, for example because of a shortage of power or raw material. Retrenchment is the permanent termination of surplus employees for reasons other than misconduct. Dismissal is termination as a punishment for serious misconduct, after due enquiry. Death also ends service.

problem.en: A firm has 200 employees. Separations run at 12% a year and it recruits 2 people a month. Will the headcount rise or fall, and at what level would it settle?

steps.en: Yearly separations at the start = 12% of 200 = 24; yearly recruits = 2 × 12 = 24.
Inflow equals outflow, so the headcount stays about 200.
In general it settles where 0.12 × H = 24, that is H = 200.
If recruitment rose to 3 a month (36 a year), it would settle at 36/0.12 = 300.

answer.en: It stays at about 200; that is its steady level.
